correctness.rationale: The crown total-domination criterion is proved in both directions, including matched nonadjacencies. Under deficit <=4, at most eight vertices are in nonsingleton blocks. Assuming one side has no singleton forces a singleton on the other side and a (r,1) coalition partner; the absence of pure blocks would require at least n>4 deficit units, while a pure block plus its necessary >=2-opposite-side partner saturates all four units and leaves at most four vertices on that side. Therefore both sides have singletons, whose disjoint distinct partners must cost at least two units each, forcing exactly opposing (2,1) and (1,2) triple blocks and no other nonsingletons. Conversely every such partition is a valid total-coalition partition. Profile-disambiguated binomial choices yield the exact count, while the union criterion yields the unique double-star partner graph. Explicit exhaustive adjacency checks for n=3..7 and all small partition witnesses support, but do not replace, this symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: Full-text analysis uncovered decisive prior scalar coverage, which is explicitly not claimed. The 2024 manuscript on double total coalitions, Proposition 3.3, and the 2025 complete-bipartite total-k-coalition result, Theorem 5.3, give the same 2n-4 optimum by a complete predicate equivalence and display opposing triple blocks; neither claims that all optimizers have that form, supplies the exact number, or proves their unique partnership graph. The Barát–Blázsik sharp-general-bound coalition-graph theorem has a nonapplicable equality hypothesis. Targeted published-finding corpus and primary literature searches found no stronger published all-extremizer coverage, but incomplete indexing and one unavailable secondary full text leave a residual novelty risk; absence of search hits alone is not treated as proof.
residual_risks: Nonindexed publications or manuscripts may contain exact maximum-partition counts not surfaced in the searches.
Henning–Jogan 2024 full text was inaccessible, although its official abstract restricts its classifications to TC=2 or graphs with a degree-one vertex; crown n>=5 lies in neither class.
Two already published results contain the same scalar and an example extremizer; independent human verification is recommended to confirm the novelty boundary of the all-extremizer theorem.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of the optimum solution space for ordinary total-coalition partitions of crown graphs: it proves extremal rigidity, a closed labeled optimizer count of order n^6, and a unique induced total-coalition graph. The first total-coalition paper explicitly proposed examining such graphs, and later works already give only the scalar and one construction. Counting and specifying all optima distinguishes many inequivalent partitions sharing one partnership graph, which is useful structural information and not an arbitrary finite-case table or marginal numerical improvement.
